verses.25:1: Julgai-me, Senhor, porque eu {ingressus} na minha inocência: * e, esperando no Senhor, {infirmabor}.
verses.25:2: Provai-me, Senhor, e {tenta}: * {ure} os meus rins e o meu coração.
verses.25:3: Porque a vossa misericórdia está diante dos meus olhos: * e {complacui}.
verses.25:4: Não me sentei com {concilium} {vanitatis}: * e com {iniqua} não entrarei.
verses.25:5: {odivi} a {ecclesiam} dos malvados: * e com os ímpios não me sentarei.
verses.25:7: Para ouvir a voz do louvor, * e narrar todas as vossas maravilhas.
verses.25:8: Senhor, amei o {decor} da vossa casa, * e {habitationis}.
verses.25:9: {perdas} com os ímpios, Deus, a minha alma, * nem com os homens de {sanguinum} a minha vida:
verses.25:10: Em cujas mãos há iniquidades: * de {muneribus} está cheia a direita deles.
verses.25:11: Mas eu {ingressus} na minha inocência: * {redime}, e tende piedade de mim.
verses.25:12: O meu pé {directo}: * nas {ecclesiis} vos bendirei, Senhor.

decisions.latin: ego in innocéntia mea ingréssus sum (25:1 = 25:11)
decisions.why: The same Latin colon twice, at the psalm's opening and near its close; one Portuguese verb for both, so that 25:11 is heard as the echo it is. ingrédi here is walking, not entering: the Greek is ἐπορεύθην (πορεύομαι, the walking verb), and the glossary row ingrédi (walking) → andar, made on Ps 14:2, names 25:1 and 25:11 ('andei na minha inocência'). entrar stays for íngredi into a place, and 25:4 introíbo already takes 'entrarei' two verses on. Douay-Rheims 'I have walked in my innocence'; Matos Soares 1932 'andei na minha inocência'.

options.label: andei
options.note: Ruling: the glossary's andar (ingrédi walking; ἐπορεύθην); both Vulgate-family versions.

options.label: entrei
options.note: The verb's first sense; 'entrei na minha inocência' says nothing in Portuguese, and collides with 25:4 introíbo → entrarei.

decisions.latin: et in Dómino sperans non infirmábor
decisions.why: infirmári: 'be weakened' (οὐ μὴ ἀσθενήσω). The glossary's note on infírmus gives the verb's family as weakness, enfraquecer (9:4 'serão enfraquecidos', 17:37 'não se enfraqueceram'); 26:2b has the same verb ('se enfraqueceram, e caíram'). The passive form is middle in sense, so the reflexive. Douay-Rheims 'shall not be weakened'; Matos Soares 1932 'não vacilarei' (another image). speráre in → esperar em (glossary).

options.label: não me enfraquecerei
options.note: Ruling: the verb of 9:4, 17:37, 26:2b, reflexive for the middle sense.

options.label: não serei enfraquecido
options.note: The passive to the letter, as 9:4 (where the Latin has an agent in view); heavier.

options.label: não vacilarei
options.note: Matos Soares 1932: another image (tottering) for the Latin's weakness — refused (rule 2).

decisions.latin: Proba me, Dómine, et tenta me
decisions.why: Two verbs of testing, δοκίμασον … πείρασον. probáre → provar (glossary examináre / probáre; 16:3 'Provastes o meu coração'). tentáre is the Latin's own word and the psalter's for Israel tempting God (77:18, 77:41, 77:56, 94:8, 105:14 — grep); 94:8 sets 'tentavérunt me … probavérunt me' side by side as here, so tentar and provar should both stay. 'tentai-me' is heard first as 'tempt me' — which the Latin word also says; the Greek πειράζω is the verb of the Lord's Prayer's temptation too. Douay-Rheims 'try me'; Matos Soares 1932 'sonda-me' (scrutári's word in this psalter). 'tentai' is safe at the vós imperative (past 'tentei').

options.label: tentai-me
options.note: Ruling: the Latin's word, apart from provar, as 94:8 needs.

options.label: ponde-me à prova
options.note: The sense 'test' without the overtone of temptation; shares the root of provar in the same colon.

options.label: sondai-me
options.note: Matos Soares 1932: scrutári's verb (glossary) — refused.

decisions.latin: ure renes meos et cor meum
decisions.why: úrere: 'burn' (L&S); the Greek πύρωσον is 'set on fire, refine by fire' — the refiner's fire, as the Latin's probáre beside it suggests. The Latin says burn, and burning is an image that must stay concrete (rule 5); 'renes' → rins (glossary: the organ named; 7:10, 15:7). The Breviary itself hears the fire literally: St Lawrence's legend applies the verse to his grilling (DO SanctiM/08-12oct.txt, grep). Douay-Rheims 'burn my reins and my heart'; Matos Soares 1932 'acrisola ao fogo os meus afectos' (explains, and loses the kidneys).

options.label: queimai
options.note: Ruling: the Latin's verb, plainly (Douay-Rheims 'burn').

options.label: abrasai
options.note: 'set ablaze'; incéndi's word in this psalter (9:23 'o pobre é abrasado').

options.label: acrisolai
options.note: Matos Soares 1932: the refiner's sense of the Greek, explained into the verb; a word few know — refused.

decisions.why: complacére in: in this psalter 'to take pleasure in' (43:4 'quóniam complacuísti in eis', God pleased with his people) — both Vulgate-family versions read 25:3 so: Douay-Rheims 'I am well pleased with thy truth', Matos Soares 1932 'na tua verdade me tenho comprazido'. The Greek εὐηρέστησα can mean 'I was well-pleasing (to you)', and the glossary's complacére → agradar was made on 18:15a, where the elóquia are to be pleasing — another build. 'comprazer-se em' keeps the Latin root and the preposition; it is a word of the Bible's own register ('em quem me comprazo', unverified in any printed Brazilian Bible — heard, not quoted).

options.label: me comprazi na vossa verdade
options.note: Ruling: took pleasure in (43:4's sense; both Vulgate-family versions); the cognate root.

options.label: me agradei da vossa verdade
options.note: The glossary's agradar in its reflexive; the preposition changes.

options.label: agradei na vossa verdade
options.note: The Greek's sense ('I was pleasing'), with the object unnamed; heard as incomplete.

decisions.why: D34 rules concílium by its Greek. Here the Greek is συνέδριον ('a sitting together, council'), neither 1:5's βουλή nor 21:17's συναγωγή, so neither assembleia nor congregação is owed — and assembleia is barred here anyway, because 25:5 has ecclésia → assembleia one verse on (two Latin words, two Greek words, ἐκκλησία in 25:5). 'conselho' is what D33 gives consílium where it is a deliberating body (110:1 'in consílio justórum et congregatióne'); συνέδριον is exactly that, a body that sits, and 'sentar-se com' makes the body plain. Cost: concílium here shares a word with consílium across the psalter (they never meet in a verse; the Latin's own manuscripts confuse the two). Douay-Rheims 'the council of vanity'; Matos Soares 1932 'na assembléia da vaidade'.

options.label: o conselho
options.note: Ruling: the deliberating body (συνέδριον), D33's word for a council.

options.label: a reunião
options.note: A word no other Latin term has; plainer, but a meeting, not a body.

options.label: a assembleia
options.note: Matos Soares 1932 (and 1:5's word): would say 25:4 and 25:5 with one word for the Latin's and the Greek's two.

options.label: a congregação
options.note: D34's word where concílium is συναγωγή (21:17) — not the Greek here.

decisions.why: vánitas → vaidade (glossary, 4:3, 118:37); ματαιότης, emptiness, falsehood. The row records that a blind reader heard 'vaidade' first as conceit; here the genitive of quality ('a council of vanity' = an empty, false council) may be heard the same way. Kept for the glossary; its option is the one the row names.

options.label: da vaidade
options.note: Ruling: the glossary's word; both Vulgate-family versions.

options.label: do que é vão
options.note: The row's option: emptiness heard first.

decisions.latin: et cum iníqua geréntibus non introíbo
decisions.why: iníqua gérere: 'to do iniquitous things' (παρανομούντων, transgressors). Not operári iniquitátem (→ praticar a iniquidade), which the Latin keeps for another build; the nearest row is Ps 24:4 iníqua ágere → agir iniquamente (open), one Latin phrase with another verb of doing. The row's word was listed unknown by one blind reader; its option is taken here as the ruling because gérere is 'to carry on, do' with a thing as object — 'fazer coisas iníquas' keeps the neuter plural object the Latin has, and 'iníquo' is the glossary's for iníquus. Douay-Rheims 'the doers of unjust things'; Matos Soares 1932 'os que praticam a iniquidade' (operári's words).

options.label: os que fazem coisas iníquas
options.note: Ruling: the Latin's neuter plural object kept (the option of the row iníqua ágere).

options.label: os que agem iniquamente
options.note: The row's word for 24:4 (ágere); an adverb for the object; 'iniquamente' unknown to one blind reader.

options.label: os que praticam a iniquidade
options.note: Matos Soares 1932: operári iniquitátem's formula — another Latin build, refused.

decisions.why: odívi is the late perfect of odio (the classical odi is a perfect with present sense — 24:19 odérunt → 'me odeiam'); the glossary row odísse gives 118:104 odívi → 'odiei'. The Greek is the aorist ἐμίσησα. The verse stands among perfects of the psalmist's past conduct (non sedi, 25:4), with futures of resolve after (non introíbo, non sedébo), so the past is the Latin's order of time. Douay-Rheims 'I have hated'; Matos Soares 1932 'Eu aborreço' (present).

options.label: Odiei
options.note: Ruling: the perfect, as 118:104; beside 'Não me sentei'.

options.label: Odeio
options.note: The present sense of classical odi (Matos Soares 1932): not this form.

decisions.why: D34: ecclésia → assembleia everywhere; 25:5 is the verse the ruling names as the reason 'igreja' cannot serve ('a igreja dos malvados'). ἐκκλησία in both (read in the parallels). The plural of 25:12 'nas assembleias' keeps the Latin's number. malignántes → malvados (D24). The psalm then says the word twice, of the wicked's gathering it hates and of the gatherings where it will bless — the Latin's own contrast, now audible.

options.label: assembleia · assembleias
options.note: Ruling: D34.

options.label: igreja · igrejas
options.note: Douay-Rheims 'churches' (25:12); refused by D34 — 'a igreja dos malvados', and 'igrejas' heard as buildings.

decisions.why: The first words of the Lavabo of the Roman Mass: the priest says Ps 25:6–12 as a unit while washing his hands, with the Gloria Patri (DO missa/Latin/Ordo/Ordo.txt, 'Ps. 25, 6-12', the text identical to the psalm's; also Ordo67 and the Holy Saturday Mass, Quad6-6). So 25:6 must stand alone as an opening, which it does. Natural Portuguese order (object before the prepositional phrase); the Latin's order ends the colon on 'as minhas mãos' and is the option. innocens → inocente (glossary). Douay-Rheims 'I will wash my hands among the innocent'. Ps 72:13 'et lavi inter innocéntes manus meas' is this colon in the perfect and should copy it ('e lavei as minhas mãos entre os inocentes').

options.label: Lavarei as minhas mãos entre os inocentes

forms.lavabo: Lavarei as minhas mãos entre os inocentes

options.note: Ruling: natural order (D2); the colon ends on a paroxytone.

options.label: Lavarei entre os inocentes as minhas mãos

forms.lavabo: Lavarei entre os inocentes as minhas mãos

options.note: The Latin's order.

decisions.why: circumdáre → cercar (glossary, working: 16:9b, 21:13), kept apart from circuíre → rodear (117:10–12), though the Greek has one verb (κυκλώσω). Ps 26:6 has 'Circuívi' two psalms on, so the two Latin verbs meet in neighbouring psalms and keep their two words. Here the one who washed his hands goes round the altar (the ritual circuit); 'cercar o altar' is heard as surrounding it, which is the Latin's picture. Douay-Rheims 'will compass thy altar'; Matos Soares 1932 'estarei ao redor do teu altar'. The Communion of Wednesday in Passion Week quotes 25:6–7 with 'circuíbo' (DO missa/Latin/Tempora/Quad5-3.txt) — another Latin text, which the Portuguese need not follow.

options.label: cercarei o vosso altar
options.note: Ruling: the glossary's circumdáre.

options.label: andarei ao redor do vosso altar

forms.circumdabo: andarei ao redor do vosso altar

options.note: The ritual circuit said outright; words added.

options.label: rodearei o vosso altar
options.note: circuíre's word (26:6): merges the two Latin verbs.

decisions.why: decor → esplendor (glossary, open; this verse is in its list). εὐπρέπεια, seemliness, comeliness. The row keeps it apart from pulchritúdo → beleza, because 95:6 and 103:1 set the two as twins. The half-verse is the versicle of the Common of the Dedication of a Church (DO Commune/C8.txt 'V. Dómine diléxi decórem domus tuæ'), so it must stand alone — it does. Douay-Rheims 'the beauty of thy house'; Matos Soares 1932 'o decoro da tua casa' (the cognate, now 'propriety').

options.label: esplendor
options.note: Ruling: the glossary's word (20:6).

options.label: beleza
options.note: Douay-Rheims; the everyday word — pulchritúdo's.

options.label: decoro
options.note: Matos Soares 1932: the cognate, heard as decorum.

decisions.why: 'the place of the dwelling of your glory' (τόπον σκηνώματος δόξης σου — σκήνωμα, a tent-dwelling). Two genitives stacked; Portuguese says the second as a clause, the glory as the subject of 'habita' — grammar (D2), no word lost: the place, the dwelling (as the verb), the glory. Matos Soares 1932 'o lugar onde habita a tua glória'; Douay-Rheims 'the place where thy glory dwelleth' — both Vulgate-family versions build it so.

options.label: o lugar onde habita a vossa glória

forms.habitationis: o lugar onde habita a vossa glória

options.note: Ruling: the noun said as a verb (both Vulgate-family versions).

options.label: o lugar da habitação da vossa glória

forms.habitationis: o lugar da habitação da vossa glória

options.note: The Latin's two genitives.

decisions.latin: Ne perdas cum ímpiis, Deus, ánimam meam
decisions.why: pérdere → fazer perecer (D24; 25:9 is in the row's list). The verse is used alone as a versicle of Passiontide ('V. Ne perdas cum ímpiis, Deus, ánimam meam. R. Et cum viris sánguinum vitam meam.' — DO Psalterium/Special/Minor Special.txt, Psalmi matutinum.txt; and the short responsory at None), so each colon must stand alone: the second begins with 'nem', which as a response still reads as the continuation it is. Deus as a bare vocative (glossary). Douay-Rheims 'Take not away my soul'; Matos Soares 1932 'Não percas'.

options.label: Não façais perecer
options.note: Ruling: D24.

options.label: Não percais
options.note: Matos Soares 1932's cognate: heard as 'do not lose' (D24).

decisions.latin: et cum viris sánguinum vitam meam
decisions.why: D29: the plural of blood → sangue; 'homens de sangue' as 5:7b. The Latinist has asked for the plural before (15:4b); held by D29. Matos Soares 1932 'os homens sanguinários'.

options.label: sangue
options.note: Ruling: D29.

options.label: sangues
options.note: The Latin's plural (the Latinist's at 15:4b), heard as a slip.

decisions.why: múnera → dádivas (glossary, open: 14:4b 'nem aceitou dádivas contra o inocente', heard as a bribe without the word). δώρων, gifts. The context makes them bribes, as in 14:4b; the word has to serve the kings' gifts too (67:30, 71:10). Douay-Rheims 'gifts'; Matos Soares 1932 'sobornos' (explains).

options.label: dádivas
options.note: Ruling: the glossary's word.

options.label: subornos
options.note: Matos Soares 1932: the sense named — explains (rule 2).

options.label: presentes
options.note: The row's option.

decisions.why: redímere → resgatar (glossary; 25:11 is in the row's list). At the vós imperative the cognate fails rule 3: 'Redimi-me' / 'Remi-me' is also 'I redeemed myself' (D13's test; 118:134 and 118:154 reached 'Resgatai-me' independently). miseréri → ter piedade (formula 'Tende piedade de mim'). The Tract of the Monday of the second week of Lent adapts it ('Rédime me, Dómine, et miserére mei', DO missa Quad2-1.txt).

options.label: resgatai-me
options.note: Ruling: the glossary's word, safe at the imperative.

options.label: remi-me
options.note: The traditional verb: its imperative is also a first-person past (rule 3).

decisions.why: in dirécto: a neuter adjective used as a noun, 'on the straight' — level ground, and uprightness (ἐν εὐθύτητι, the Greek word behind diréctio 'retidão' in 118:7). The Latin leaves both, the place and the virtue, and names no road. Douay-Rheims and Matos Soares 1932 both add a way ('in the direct way', 'no caminho recto'), as does the Lenten Tract that adapts the verse ('pes enim meus stetit in via recta', DO missa Quad2-1.txt) — another text. 'no que é reto' keeps the adjective and both senses. stare: the glossary's 'estar de pé' cannot be said of a foot; 'esteve firme' keeps the posture of stetit (stood, did not slip).

options.label: esteve firme no que é reto

forms.directo: esteve firme no que é reto

options.note: Ruling: the adjective kept, place and virtue both audible; 'firme' carries stetit.

options.label: esteve firme no caminho reto
options.note: Both Vulgate-family versions add 'way': decides for the place.

options.label: esteve firme na retidão
options.note: The Greek's noun (εὐθύτης = diréctio, 118:7 'retidão'): decides for the virtue.

choices.25:1: Júdica me → 'Julgai-me', bare (glossary judicáre; 7:9b opens the same way). quóniam ego → 'porque eu': the pronoun kept for the Latin's emphasis, which 25:11 'Ego autem' answers ('Mas eu'). The Latin's order of the participle kept ('e, esperando no Senhor, …').
choices.25:3: ante óculos meos → 'diante dos meus olhos'.
choices.25:4: sedére cum → 'sentar-se com'; introíre → entrar (glossary íngredi / intráre).
choices.25:5: malignántes → malvados (D24). sedébo → 'não me sentarei', the verb of 25:4 again, as the Latin repeats it.
choices.25:6: The Lavabo (25:6–12) begins here; each verse of it reads alone as well as in the psalm. The colon's final ':' is DO's (25:7 is its purpose clause).
choices.25:7: ut áudiam … et enárrem → 'Para ouvir … e narrar': the purpose infinitives (the subject is the speaker's own). vocem laudis → 'a voz do louvor' (laus → louvor). enarráre → narrar (glossary), mirabília → 'maravilhas' (the family of mirábilis).
choices.25:10: In quorum mánibus iniquitátes sunt → 'Em cujas mãos há iniquidades' ('há' for sunt, as Portuguese says existence). déxtera → 'a direita' (glossary); 'deles' rather than 'sua', so that it is not heard as God's (named in 25:9). repléta est → 'está cheia'. The second colon is turned ('de dádivas está cheia a direita deles') so that the verse does not end on the proparoxytone 'dádivas' (rule 4; checks.py flag on the first order, 'a direita deles está cheia de dádivas', which is the order of speech).
choices.25:11: Ego autem → 'Mas eu' (glossary; 16:15). The first colon is 25:1's words, the verse ending on 'inocência' in both.
choices.25:12: benedícere (man → God), accusative → 'vos bendirei' (glossary). The Tract of Monday in the second week of Lent adapts this verse with other words ('Rédime me … pes enim meus stetit in via recta: in ecclésiis benedícam Dóminum') — not this psalm's Latin.

audit.note: Latin = DO Psalm25.txt, twelve prayed verses, ids 25:1–25:12 (none repeated), no flex. No titulus (D7). DO's other uses, grep-checked (ps025/grep_do.py): the Lavabo of the Mass is 25:6–12 whole, identical to the psalm (Ordo.txt, Ordo67.txt, Quad6-6.txt); the Communion of Wednesday in Passion Week quotes 25:6–7 in another Latin ('circuíbo', 'laudis tuæ'); 25:1 is the Introit of Monday in the second week of Lent (Quad2-1.txt) and 25:11–12 is adapted in its Tract; 25:8a is the versicle of the Common of the Dedication (Commune/C8.txt); 25:9 is the Passiontide versicle and short responsory ('Ne perdas cum ímpiis, Deus, ánimam meam. R. Et cum viris sánguinum vitam meam', Minor Special.txt, Psalmi matutinum.txt, Tempora/Quad5-2.txt); 25:12b is a versicle in a local office (10-23-Redemptor.txt); 25:2 is applied to St Lawrence in a lesson (SanctiM/08-12oct.txt).

Psalm-level draft from consult/parallels/ps025.md (Latin, LXX, WLC, Douay-Rheims, Matos Soares 1932; no Diurnal text for this psalm). DO's Portuguese not used (D12). Settled words applied: D24 pérdere (25:9), malignántes (25:5); D29 sangue (25:9); D34 ecclésia → assembleia (25:5, 25:12) and concílium by its Greek (25:4, συνέδριον: 'conselho'). Repeats found with ps005/grep_latin.py: concílium 3 lines (1:5, 25:4, 39:11), vánitas genitive only here, innocéntia / innocens 18 lines (72:13 'lavi inter innocéntes manus meas' is 25:6a's twin), tentáre 7 lines, complacére 7 lines, 'in dirécto' only here. Latin readings kept against the Hebrew: 25:3 'me comprazi na vossa verdade' (not 'I walked'), 25:5 'assembleia' is the Latin's and the Greek's, 25:10 'iniquidades' (not 'a plot'). The Lavabo (25:6–12) checked to stand alone verse by verse. 19 decisions.

Draft 1: hard pass. Soft flags accepted: 25:1 first colon −7 and 25:11 first colon −5 (the Latin's 'ingréssus sum' and 'innocéntia mea' are long; the Portuguese is 'andei na minha inocência'); 25:1 second colon +3; 25:7 second colon −3; 25:12 first colon +4 ('esteve firme no que é reto' for 'stetit in dirécto'). Rhyme 25:4 / 25:5 'entrarei / sentarei' at the finals: the Latin's own echo of futures (introíbo / sedébo), and the second is the Latin's verb of 25:4 repeated — kept. 25:10 turned so as not to end on the proparoxytone 'dádivas' (flagged on the first order).
